summary: Robert F. Rhodes is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology. A doctoral candidate at Harvard University, he served as a professor at Otani University, attested during 1993–2000 and 2012–2014.

Robert Florida works in religious and Buddhist studies. He served as Dean of Arts and Professor of Religion at Brandon University and was an Emeritus Fellow at the University of Victoria (attested 2000–2005).

Robert Ford Campany is a sinologist and religious studies scholar. He was a professor at Indiana University Bloomington (~1989–2006), taught at the University of Southern California (~2006–2010), and became a colleague at Vanderbilt University in 2010.

Robert Gardner (1925–2014) earned his BA from Harvard University (~1943–1947). He served as an assistant at the Fogg Museum, taught at the University of Puget Sound, founded Harvard University in 1957, and was a professor there (1956–1997).

Robert Gauthiot (1876–1916) specialized in Iranian and Central Asian studies, linguistics, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1898–1904) and became a member of the Société Asiatique in 1909.
Robert Göbl (1919–1997) worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies and history/archaeology. He studied at the University of Vienna (1947–1950) and later held a post there from circa 1955 to 1989.

Robert H. Brower (1923–1988) was a Japanologist who studied at Harvard and Michigan. He held posts at Minnesota, Stanford, and the Inter-University Center for Japanese Language Studies, and chaired Far Eastern Languages and Literatures at Michigan (1966–1988).

Robert H. Sharf, a Buddhist studies scholar, sinologist, and Japanologist, earned degrees from Toronto and Michigan and studied at Kyoto. He taught at McMaster and Michigan before becoming D. H. Chen Distinguished Professor at UC Berkeley (~2004).
Robert Hinde (1923–2016) studied at St John's College (~1941–1948) and Balliol College, Oxford (~1948–1950). He held an academic post at the University of Cambridge from circa 1950 to 1989.

Robert J. Miller (1923–1994) specialized in Buddhist studies and Indology. He served as a professor on the faculty of the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1955–1989) and as a professor at the American Institute of Indian Studies.
Robert J. Topmiller specializes in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Kentucky under the supervision of George C. Herring.

Robert Kritzer is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed his PhD at the University of California, Berkeley (1995) under Padmanabh S. Jaini and served as Associate Professor at Kyoto Notre Dame University (attested 1999–2017).

Robert L. Brown (1943–2014) worked in Indology, history/archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He was a South and Southeast Asian art curator at the Los Angeles County Museum of Art (~1983–2014) and professor emeritus at UCLA (~1986–2014).

Robert Lenz (1808–1836) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Tartu and Berlin under Franz Bopp. He taught at the Cathedral School of Tallinn and served as Professor of Sanskrit at Saint Petersburg State University (~1835–1836).

Robert M. Gimello (1942–2020) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology who earned his PhD at Columbia (~1968–1976). He headed Oriental Studies and was professor emeritus at Arizona (~1981–2020) and taught at Harvard (~2002–2006).

Robert Maclagan (1820–1894) was an Indologist and historian who studied at Edinburgh, Addiscombe Military Seminary, and the Royal School of Military Engineering. He served as Principal of the Indian Institute of Technology Roorkee from 1847 to 1860.

Robert Magliola earned his PhD at Princeton (~1965–1970). A scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and religious studies, he held posts at Purdue, Tamkang, Assumption, National Taiwan University, and Columbia University.

Robert Mayer specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He completed a dissertation at Bristol and a PhD at Leiden under Tilmann Vetter, Alexis Sanderson, and Pieter Cornelis Verhagen, joining Oxford's Oriental Studies Faculty in 2002.

Robert Needham Cust (1821–1909) was a linguist and Indologist. He studied at Eton, Trinity College Cambridge, East India Company College, and Fort William College, and served in the Bengal Civil Service from circa 1843 to 1867.

Robert P. Goldman is an Indologist who studied at Columbia and Penn under Ludo Rocher. Beginning in ~1971, he served as a professor at the University of California, Berkeley, where he is attested as Professor Emeritus in 2026.
